intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the fleeting sakura season, and stroll the lantern-lit paths at dusk. Families can enjoy street food stalls selling takoyaki and dango surrounding the park.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon), explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks, and let kids try on samurai and kimono costumes at nearby rental shops. A perfect blend of history and family fun.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and educational experience for families, the Peace Memorial Museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, and promotes a message of global peace. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, see the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and fold paper cranes at the Children's Peace Monument. A historically significant and emotionally enriching visit.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture with a self-guided or guided tour of the Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), matcha ice cream, and grilled seafood skewers. Kids and adults alike will love the vibrant atmosphere and the chance to taste authentic Japanese street food at its finest.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Cross the scenic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River, visit the nearby Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and spot wild monkeys at Iwatayama Monkey Park. A perfect full-day family adventure combining nature, culture, and history.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: After clearing customs and collecting luggage, take the airport limousine bus or local train to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront area to get oriented. Enjoy the coastal scenery and nearby cherry blossom trees if still in bloom in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate neighborhood around the resort. Visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) to stock up on budget-friendly snacks and drinks. Take an evening walk along the beach to unwind after the long flight.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip
meals.lunch: Grab an onigiri (rice ball) or bento box from a convenience store near the airport for around ¥300–¥600
meals.dinner: Visit a nearby gyudon (beef bowl) chain like Yoshinoya or Sukiya — hearty meal for ¥400–¥700

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to arrival at 13:00 and potential jet lag. Get a Suica or PASMO IC card at the airport for easy train and bus travel throughout the trip. Exchange some yen at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the nearest local park or shrine famous for cherry blossoms. Enjoy a traditional hanami (flower viewing) picnic under the sakura trees. Pack convenience store snacks and drinks for a budget-friendly outdoor breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby historical district or old town area. Visit a free or low-cost local museum or cultural center to learn about the region's history. Look for traditional craft shops and local markets.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free evening illumination event if cherry blossoms are still lit up at night (yozakura). Many parks offer free nighttime cherry blossom viewing in April.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri and green tea — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Picnic under cherry blossoms with convenience store bento boxes and snacks — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Ramen shop dinner — a filling bowl of ramen costs ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April cherry blossoms may be in late bloom or petal-fall stage (hanafubuki), which is equally beautiful. Check local bloom forecasts online. Bring a picnic mat from a 100-yen shop (Daiso) for the hanami.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local train to a nearby historic castle or temple complex. Many castles in Japan charge ¥500–¥800 entry and offer stunning views and historical exhibits perfect for families and history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the castle town or surrounding historic streets (often called 'jo-shita-machi'). Browse local souvenir shops and try regional street food snacks. Visit a traditional garden if available nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and visit a local izakaya (Japanese pub) for affordable shared dishes. Great for experiencing authentic Japanese culture with the family.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or convenience store pastry and coffee — ¥200–¥400
meals.lunch: Street food near the castle town — try takoyaki or yakitori skewers for ¥300–¥600
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner with shared plates — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Many castles offer discounts for children under 12 or free entry for young children. Check the castle's official website before visiting. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a famous Shinto shrine in the region. Participate in the morning ritual atmosphere, try your luck with omikuji (fortune slips) for ¥100–¥200, and admire the torii gate architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a traditional Japanese craft workshop or cultural experience such as a pottery class, origami workshop, or calligraphy session. Many community centers offer these for ¥500–¥1,500.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local onsen (hot spring public bath) for a relaxing soak. Public sento baths are very affordable at ¥400–¥800 per person and are a quintessential Japanese cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Tamago kake gohan (raw egg on rice) set at a local diner — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Soba noodle restaurant near the shrine — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Teishoku (set meal) at a family restaurant like Gusto or Denny's Japan — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: At the onsen, note that tattoos may be prohibited at some facilities. Bring a small towel or rent one for ¥100–¥200. Children typically pay a reduced entry fee at public baths.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local train to a nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site or nationally significant historical landmark. Japan has numerous such sites accessible by regional rail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the heritage site, including its surrounding temples, pagodas, or ancient streets. Many areas have free outdoor walking paths and gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Pick up regional specialty foods from a local supermarket or depachika (department store basement food hall) for a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast sandwich and canned coffee — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Packed bento from a local supermarket near the heritage site — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Supermarket or depachika prepared foods (sushi packs, salads, side dishes) — ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Use your IC card (Suica/PASMO) for train travel to save time. Many heritage sites have free entry for the outdoor grounds with optional paid entry to specific buildings. Download Google Maps offline for navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at a local beach or coastal park near the resort. Enjoy the spring sea breeze, collect shells, and take family photos with the ocean backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local aquarium or nature center if available in the area — great for families with children. Many regional aquariums charge ¥1,000–¥2,000 per adult with discounts for children.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the beach or a nearby elevated point. Bring convenience store snacks and enjoy the golden hour sky as a free family activity.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or seaside café morning set — ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local fish market or port-side restaurant — ¥800–¥1,200 for a seafood bowl (kaisen-don)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using supermarket ingredients if the accommodation has a kitchenette, or grab sushi from a conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi) restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Mid-April sea temperatures in Japan are still cool, so swimming is not recommended. The beach is best for walks and relaxation. Check if the aquarium offers family bundle tickets for savings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local farmers' market or morning market (asaichi). These are common in Japanese coastal towns and offer fresh produce, local foods, and cultural interaction with vendors at very low cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a historic neighborhood or preserved traditional townscape (machiya district). Walk through narrow lanes lined with old wooden merchant houses and small local museums.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free local community event, festival, or temple evening ceremony if available. Check local tourism boards for April cultural events.

meals.breakfast: Sample fresh foods at the morning market — ¥300–¥600
meals.lunch: Local udon restaurant — a large bowl of udon costs ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set meal at a local restaurant — ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Farmers' markets in Japan typically run from 6:00–10:00 AM, so plan accordingly. Bring cash as many small vendors do not accept cards. The machiya districts are excellent for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a renowned Buddhist temple complex in the region. Explore the main hall, sub-temples, and meditation gardens. Many temples offer free or low-cost entry to outdoor grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a zazen (seated meditation) experience if offered by the temple — many temples run beginner sessions for ¥500–¥1,000. A unique cultural and calming activity for families.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a 100-yen shop (Daiso) for affordable souvenir shopping — great for picking up unique Japanese items like stationery, kitchen goods, and small gifts at ¥100–¥300 each.

meals.breakfast: Shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) tasting set if offered at the temple — ¥800–¥1,200, or convenience store alternative
meals.lunch: Vegetarian tofu restaurant near the temple district — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Yakiniku (grilled meat) at a budget chain restaurant — ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Dress respectfully when visiting temples — covered shoulders and knees are appreciated. Remove shoes when entering temple buildings. The zazen session may require advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated souvenir and cultural shopping day. Visit a local covered shopping arcade (shotengai) for authentic, locally made crafts, traditional sweets (wagashi), and regional specialties at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a hands-on cultural museum or open-air folk museum where visitors can try traditional activities like weaving, rice cake pounding (mochi tsuki), or traditional toy making — ideal for families.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a nicer but still budget-friendly restaurant. Try a regional specialty dish unique to the area you've been staying in.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store morning set — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Takoyaki, crepes, or other street food in the shopping arcade — ¥400–¥700
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant featuring regional cuisine — ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person as a treat

day_by_day.notes: Budget ¥3,000–¥8,000 for souvenir shopping depending on your needs. Popular budget souvenir items include matcha Kit Kats, regional sembei (rice crackers), tenugui (hand towels), and small kokeshi dolls. Wrap fragile items carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk along the beach or through a nearby cherry blossom park for last photos and memories. Return to the resort to pack and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with ample time. Use remaining yen at the airport for last-minute snacks, food, or duty-free shopping. Return or top up your IC card if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations and final reflections on the trip. Enjoy an airport meal featuring Japanese cuisine one last time before flying home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or final convenience store breakfast — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Airport food court meal — ramen, soba, or udon available at most Japanese airports for ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. If you have leftover coins, spend them at airport vending machines or donate to charity boxes at the airport. Unused IC card balance can be refunded at airport service counters.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the fleeting sakura season, and stroll the lantern-lit paths at dusk. Families can enjoy street food stalls selling takoyaki and dango surrounding the park.

A perfect blend of history and family fun.

experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. A perfect full-day family adventure combining nature, culture, and history.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange transport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Take the airport express train or a mid-range shared shuttle to your beachfront accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to orient yourself. Visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) to pick up snacks and essentials — a quintessential Japanese experience in itself.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first dinner near the hotel to recover from jet lag. Explore the local neighborhood, find a family-friendly izakaya or casual Japanese restaurant nearby, and enjoy an early night to adjust to the time zone.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store bento box (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near the hotel — try yakitori, edamame, and miso soup (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: April 15 is peak cherry blossom season in many parts of Japan. Keep expectations light for Day 1 — rest is the priority. Exchange some yen at the airport if you haven't already, and pick up a prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo) for easy transit.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Tokyo's Asakusa district for a visit to Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Arrive early (around 8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and explore the temple grounds. The surrounding streets will have beautiful cherry blossoms in bloom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Nakamise Shopping Street, the traditional market lane leading to Senso-ji, and pick up souvenirs, traditional snacks (ningyo-yaki, senbei), and small gifts. Afterward, walk along the Sumida River embankment where cherry blossom trees line the riverbank — a stunning hanami backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Take the train to Shibuya or Shinjuku for dinner. Explore the vibrant evening atmosphere, visit a department store food basement (depachika) for a preview of Japanese food culture, then enjoy dinner at a mid-range ramen or tempura restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery/café (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Nakamise Street snacks and a sit-down meal at a local soba or tempura restaurant in Asakusa (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Ramen shop or tonkatsu restaurant in Shinjuku (¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Nakamise Street opens around 10:00 AM. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Sumida River cherry blossom walk is especially beautiful in mid-April and is free to enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market for a self-guided food tour. Arrive around 8:00–9:00 AM when stalls are at their freshest and most lively. Sample fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (Japanese egg omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha treats. This is a fantastic cultural and culinary experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 per adult, free for children under 6), a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a tea house on a pond — perfect for a peaceful cultural afternoon. Enjoy a cup of matcha tea with a traditional wagashi sweet in the garden teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short walk or train to Ginza for window shopping and a family-friendly dinner. Ginza has excellent mid-range dining options including conveyor-belt sushi (kaiten-zushi), which children especially love.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, and green tea (¥1,000–¥2,000 per person)
meals.lunch: Light snacks from Tsukiji stalls or a casual lunch at a nearby teishoku (set meal) restaurant (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) in Ginza — great for families (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best visited early. Most stalls are open by 8:00 AM and can get very crowded by 10:00 AM on weekends. Hamarikyu Gardens is a hidden gem and rarely overcrowded — a wonderful contrast to the busy market.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi or Hikari line. Book seats in advance using a Japan Rail Pass or purchase tickets at the station. Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning and check in or store luggage at your Kyoto accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head straight to Maruyama Park for the iconic Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) is a breathtaking centerpiece. Spread out a picnic blanket, purchase bento boxes from nearby stalls, and soak in the magical atmosphere under the blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic Gion district on foot as evening falls — lanterns illuminate the traditional machiya townhouses and you may spot a geiko or maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to an engagement. Enjoy a kaiseki-inspired set dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Gion.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a convenience store onigiri and coffee before departing Tokyo (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Bento box and street food from Maruyama Park vendors (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Set menu dinner (teishoku or kaiseki-lite) in Gion — try tofu cuisine or kaiseki set (¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance, especially on weekends during cherry blossom season — trains fill up quickly. Maruyama Park is free to enter and is one of the best hanami spots in all of Japan. Evening in Gion is magical and family-friendly as long as you are respectful of residents.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove early in the morning (before 9:00 AM) to experience the towering bamboo forest with minimal crowds. Walk through the ethereal green tunnels and listen to the rustling of the bamboo — a truly unforgettable sensory experience for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River, framed by cherry-blossom-covered mountains — one of Japan's most iconic landscape views. Explore Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning garden (¥500 per adult), a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Rent a rowboat on the river for a fun family activity (¥1,500–¥2,000 per boat).
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto and visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's narrow covered market known as 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Browse dozens of stalls selling pickles, grilled skewers, fresh tofu, and local delicacies. Have dinner at a nearby izakaya in the Kawaramachi area.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading to Arashiyama (hotel breakfast or convenience store)
meals.lunch: Riverside café or restaurant in Arashiyama — try yudofu (tofu hot pot) or soba noodles (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Izakaya in Kawaramachi — share small plates of yakitori, gyoza, and seasonal vegetables (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is extremely crowded by mid-morning — an early start is essential. The bamboo grove is free to walk through. Tenryu-ji garden requires a separate admission. Nishiki Market stalls typically close by 6:00–7:00 PM, so plan the market visit in the early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Fushimi Inari Taisha, the famous Shinto shrine famous for its thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the mountain. Start early to avoid crowds. The full hike to the summit takes 2–3 hours, but families can enjoy the lower gates and turn back at any point. Free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nijo Castle (¥1,030 per adult, reduced for children), a stunning 17th-century shogun palace with 'nightingale floors' that squeak to alert guards of intruders — a fascinating history lesson for children. The castle grounds also feature beautiful cherry blossom trees in April.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening near Kyoto Station. Visit the Kyoto Tower observation deck for panoramic city views at dusk (¥900 per adult), then have dinner at one of the many excellent restaurants in the Kyoto Station building.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before heading to Fushimi Inari — hotel or convenience store (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Small restaurant or food stall near Fushimi Inari — try inari sushi (fried tofu pouches with rice, named after the shrine) (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Kyoto Station building — wide range of options from ramen to sushi to Kyoto-style cuisine (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is open 24 hours and free. Nijo Castle is closed on Tuesdays in some months — verify the schedule before visiting and swap with another attraction if needed. The nightingale floors at Nijo Castle are a huge hit with children.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 45 minutes on the Nozomi). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a deeply moving and educational experience for families. The museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, with powerful exhibits and personal testimonies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, visit the Atomic Bomb Dome (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and pay respects at the Children's Peace Monument adorned with thousands of origami cranes. Take a short ferry (¥180 each way) to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Miyajima Island at dusk when the day-trippers have left and the atmosphere becomes serene. Watch the torii gate reflect in the water at high tide. Return to Hiroshima for dinner and try Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki — a savory layered pancake unique to the region.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick bite at Kyoto Station before departing (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Light meal near the Peace Park — try Hiroshima-style tsukemen or a bento (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Hiroshima okonomiyaki at a local okonomiyaki restaurant — a must-try regional specialty (¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum (¥200 per adult, free for children under 18) is sobering but important — prepare children in advance with age-appropriate context. Miyajima ferry is included with the JR Pass. The floating torii is best seen at high tide — check tide times in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo by Shinkansen from Hiroshima (approximately 4 hours on the Nozomi). Use the journey time to relax, enjoy bento boxes from the station, and watch the Japanese countryside pass by — itself a cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tokyo and visit Ueno Park, one of Japan's most famous hanami spots. With late-blooming cherry varieties, blossoms may still be visible in mid-April. Explore the Ueno Zoo (¥600 per adult, ¥200 for children) — Japan's oldest zoo, home to giant pandas — a perfect family activity.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Akihabara (Electric Town) for a fascinating evening of Japanese pop culture, anime, electronics, and gaming arcades. Families with children will love the multi-floor game centers. Have dinner at a themed café or a casual restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Station bento (ekiben) purchased at Hiroshima Station before boarding the Shinkansen (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Ueno Park — purchase bento from nearby convenience store or market stall (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Casual restaurant in Akihabara — try a maid café experience or a family ramen restaurant (¥1,200–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance for the Hiroshima-Tokyo route. Ueno Park is free to enter; the zoo requires a ticket. Akihabara is safe and family-friendly in the early evening. The multi-floor game arcades (like Taito Station or Sega) are free to enter, with individual games costing ¥100–¥200.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (or its satellite facility if undergoing renovation) to explore 400 years of Tokyo's history through impressive scale models, artifacts, and interactive exhibits — perfect for history lovers and children alike. Nearby Ryogoku is also home to sumo culture — check if a morning sumo practice (keiko) viewing is available at a local stable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Odaiba, a futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay, accessible by the scenic Yurikamome monorail. Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book tickets in advance, approximately ¥3,200 per adult) — an immersive digital art experience that is spectacular for families. Alternatively, explore the Toyota Mega Web or the free Odaiba beach area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views over Tokyo Bay and the Rainbow Bridge from Odaiba. Have dinner at a restaurant in the Aqua City or DiverCity shopping malls on Odaiba, with views of the illuminated Rainbow Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Restaurant near the Edo-Tokyo Museum in Ryogoku — try chanko nabe (sumo wrestlers' hot pot stew), a local specialty (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Odaiba's Aqua City or DiverCity mall — wide variety of cuisines available (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets well in advance online — they frequently sell out, especially on weekends. The Yurikamome monorail ride to Odaiba is itself a fun experience with great views of the bay. Sumo stable visits typically require advance arrangements through a local guide or hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — visit Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku, a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. The forested walk to the shrine is peaceful and beautiful, a perfect final cultural moment. Afterward, stroll down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for quirky Japanese street fashion, crepes, and colorful snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shibuya for last-minute shopping and the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian crossing. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000 per adult) for sweeping 360-degree views of Tokyo as a memorable farewell to the city. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final farewell dinner at a special restaurant — splurge slightly for the last night. Try a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant where you cook thinly sliced beef in a communal hot pot at the table — a celebratory and interactive dining experience. Head to the airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it leisurely on the final morning (included or ¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepes and street food on Takeshita Street — a fun, casual, and very Japanese experience (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant in Shibuya — a memorable farewell meal (¥3,000–¥5,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transit and check-in. Store luggage at the hotel or use a coin locker at Shibuya Station. The Shibuya Sky observation deck requires timed entry tickets — book online in advance. Consider purchasing final omiyage (souvenir gifts) at the airport duty-free or at a depachika (department store basement food hall) in Shibuya.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the fleeting sakura season, and stroll the lantern-lit paths at dusk. Families can enjoy street food stalls selling takoyaki and dango surrounding the park.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon), explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks, and let kids try on samurai and kimono costumes at nearby rental shops. A perfect blend of history and family fun.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and educational experience for families, the Peace Memorial Museum chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, and promotes a message of global peace. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, see the iconic A-Bomb Dome, and fold paper cranes at the Children's Peace Monument. A historically significant and emotionally enriching visit.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture with a self-guided or guided tour of the Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), matcha ice cream, and grilled seafood skewers. Kids and adults alike will love the vibrant atmosphere and the chance to taste authentic Japanese street food at its finest.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Cross the scenic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River, visit the nearby Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and spot wild monkeys at Iwatayama Monkey Park. A perfect full-day family adventure combining nature, culture, and history.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Settle into your beachfront suite and refresh after the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Orientation & Leisure — Explore the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds, enjoy the beachfront terrace, and unwind with a welcome amenity. Take a gentle stroll along the coastline to acclimate to Japan's timezone and atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Dinner at the Resort — Enjoy a leisurely kaiseki-inspired welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the waterfront. Toast to the beginning of your Japan journey with premium sake or Japanese whisky.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments upon arrival at the resort's lounge — seasonal Japanese snacks, matcha, and fresh fruit platters
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — multi-course kaiseki dinner featuring seasonal spring ingredients, premium wagyu, and fresh seafood paired with curated sake selections

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance to ensure the suite is ready upon arrival. Ask the concierge to arrange the full 10-day itinerary briefing over welcome drinks. April 15 falls during peak cherry blossom season — confirm all Kyoto and Tokyo bookings are secured.

day_by_day.morning: Resort Spa & Onsen Morning — Begin the day with a private onsen session and a rejuvenating treatment at the resort spa. This gentle start allows the family to recover from jet lag before the cultural immersion begins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Local Coastal Village Exploration — Take a private guided tour of the nearest historic coastal town. Visit a local Shinto shrine, browse artisan craft shops, and observe traditional fishing culture along the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Private Teppanyaki Experience — Enjoy an exclusive teppanyaki dinner arranged by the resort, featuring A5 wagyu beef, Hokkaido scallops, and seasonal vegetables prepared tableside by a master chef.

meals.breakfast: In-suite Japanese breakfast — miso soup, grilled fish, tamagoyaki, rice, pickles, and freshly brewed green tea delivered to your beachfront terrace
meals.lunch: Casual seaside lunch at a curated local restaurant — fresh sashimi, tempura, and cold soba noodles with ocean views
meals.dinner: Private teppanyaki dinner at the resort — A5 wagyu, Hokkaido scallops, lobster, and seasonal vegetables with premium Japanese whisky pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa session the evening prior to secure preferred time slots. The local village tour pairs wonderfully with a rickshaw or e-bike rental for families with children. Confirm dietary preferences with the teppanyaki chef in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen Journey to Kyoto — Depart by private transfer to the nearest Shinkansen station and board a reserved Green Car (first class) bullet train to Kyoto. Arrive mid-morning and check into a luxury ryokan in the Higashiyama district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Experience the magical hanami tradition beneath Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Stroll through the park with a private guide who explains the cultural significance of hanami. The peak bloom in mid-April creates a breathtaking pink canopy overhead.
day_by_day.evening: Gion District Evening Walk — Explore the lantern-lit cobblestone streets of Gion, Kyoto's historic geisha district. With luck and a private guide's connections, enjoy a rare ozashiki (geisha banquet) experience at a traditional ochaya teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — full Japanese spread with seasonal miso soup, grilled fish, and local pickles
meals.lunch: Picnic-style hanami lunch in Maruyama Park — premium bento boxes curated by the ryokan featuring seasonal Kyoto cuisine (kyoto-style pickles, yuba, and sakura mochi)
meals.dinner: Ozashiki dinner at a private Gion ochaya teahouse — multi-course kaiseki with geisha entertainment, or alternatively, dinner at Kikunoi Honten (three Michelin stars) in Higashiyama

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is extremely popular on weekends in cherry blossom season — arrive before 11:00 AM to enjoy it before crowds peak. The ozashiki experience requires advance booking weeks ahead and is arranged through the ryokan concierge. Dress in smart casual or traditional yukata provided by the ryokan.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Togetsukyo Bridge — Journey to Arashiyama for an early morning private walk through the ethereal bamboo forest before the day-trip crowds arrive. The towering green stalks create a cathedral-like atmosphere unique to Japan. Cross the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge with views of cherry blossoms framing the Oi River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tenryu-ji Temple and Zen Garden — Visit the UNESCO-listed Tenryu-ji Temple and its exquisite Sogenchi Garden, one of Japan's oldest and finest Zen gardens. Participate in a private zazen (seated meditation) session guided by a resident monk.
day_by_day.evening: Nishiki Market & Pontocho Alley Dinner — Visit Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for a guided tasting tour of local delicacies. Head to the atmospheric Pontocho alley for a private kaiseki dinner at a riverside restaurant with tatami seating.

meals.breakfast: Traditional ryokan breakfast — full multi-dish Japanese morning meal served in your room or the tatami dining hall
meals.lunch: Shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) lunch at Tenryu-ji's Shigetsu restaurant — an extraordinary cultural and culinary experience within the temple grounds
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at a premium Pontocho restaurant — seasonal Kyoto cuisine with tofu specialties, river fish, and wagyu, with sake pairing overlooking the Kamo River

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is best experienced before 8:00 AM — arrange an early private car with the ryokan. The bamboo grove is free to enter. Book Tenryu-ji zazen session in advance through the concierge. Pontocho restaurants have limited seating; reservations are essential during cherry blossom season.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — Visit the iconic Fushimi Inari Shrine at dawn for a transcendent experience walking through thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the forested mountainside. A private guide provides historical context about the Inari deity and fox symbolism. Climb as high as your family's energy allows for panoramic views over Kyoto.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nijo Castle & Imperial Palace Grounds — Explore the historic Nijo Castle, the opulent Edo-period residence of the Tokugawa shoguns, famous for its 'nightingale floors' that squeak to detect intruders. Stroll the Imperial Palace grounds and East Garden with a licensed cultural guide.
day_by_day.evening: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) Twilight Visit & Farewell Kyoto Dinner — Arrange a private after-hours viewing of the Golden Pavilion reflected in Kyoto's cherry blossom-tinged dusk (subject to special access). Celebrate Kyoto with a farewell dinner at a top-tier restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the ryokan before the Fushimi Inari dawn visit — rice porridge, pickles, and green tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a refined Fushimi area restaurant — Kyoto-style ramen, tofu hot pot, or seasonal bento in a traditional townhouse setting
meals.dinner: Farewell Kyoto kaiseki dinner at Nakamura (one of Kyoto's oldest and most prestigious kaiseki restaurants, established 1716) — full seasonal tasting menu with premium sake

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari at sunrise (around 5:30–6:00 AM in April) is a magical and crowd-free experience — plan accordingly. Private after-hours Golden Pavilion access may require special arrangements through a premium travel concierge. Pack comfortable walking shoes for Fushimi Inari's mountain trails.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen to Hiroshima — Depart Kyoto by Green Car Shinkansen to Hiroshima (approximately 1.5 hours). Check into a luxury hotel in central Hiroshima. The journey itself offers stunning views of the Japanese countryside and Seto Inland Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — A deeply moving and educational experience for the whole family. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum, which chronicles the events of August 6, 1945, with thoughtful, age-appropriate guidance from a private historian guide. Walk through Peace Memorial Park, visit the Atomic Bomb Dome (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and participate in the tradition of folding origami paper cranes at the Children's Peace Monument.
day_by_day.evening: Miyajima Island Sunset Excursion — Take a short ferry to the sacred island of Miyajima to see the iconic 'floating' Otorii gate of Itsukushima Shrine glowing at sunset. Stroll the shrine corridors over the water and observe free-roaming sacred deer. Return to Hiroshima for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast before checkout or a premium in-hotel breakfast in Kyoto
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory pancake with noodles) at a renowned local restaurant — an authentic regional specialty not to be missed
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner in Hiroshima featuring Hiroshima oysters (among Japan's finest) — kaiseki or omakase at a top-rated local restaurant near the Peace Park

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is a profound experience — allow at least 2–3 hours and prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. The museum is respectful and educational rather than graphic. Miyajima's floating torii gate is particularly spectacular at high tide — check tide times with the hotel concierge. Book the Miyajima ferry and shrine access in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Miyajima Deep Dive — Return to Miyajima Island for a full morning exploration. Hike to the summit of Mount Misen via ropeway and trail for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea and surrounding islands. Visit Daisho-in Temple, one of Japan's most important Shingon Buddhist temples, filled with fascinating statues and prayer wheels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shinkansen to Tokyo — Depart Hiroshima by Green Car Shinkansen to Tokyo (approximately 4 hours on the Nozomi). Settle into your luxury Tokyo hotel — ideally in Marunouchi, Ginza, or Shinjuku — with views of the city skyline or Mount Fuji on clear days.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Arrival & Skyline Dinner — After settling in, enjoy a panoramic dinner at a sky-high Tokyo restaurant. Take in the glittering city lights from above as an introduction to one of the world's greatest metropolises.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast in Hiroshima — full Japanese or Western spread with fresh local produce
meals.lunch: Bento boxes in Green Car on the Shinkansen — curated premium ekiben (station bento) purchased at Hiroshima Station featuring regional specialties
meals.dinner: Sky-high dinner at a renowned Tokyo restaurant — consider Signature at Mandarin Oriental Tokyo (French-Japanese fusion) or Kozue at Park Hyatt Tokyo (traditional Japanese with Mount Fuji views)

day_by_day.notes: The Shinkansen journey from Hiroshima to Tokyo passes through some stunning scenery including a glimpse of Mount Fuji on clear afternoons — sit on the right side (seat D or E) for the best views. Book the Tokyo luxury hotel well in advance as April is peak season. Confirm Mount Fuji visibility forecasts with the hotel upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street — Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple in the historic Asakusa district. Arrive early to experience the temple in a more serene atmosphere. Walk through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft shops, try ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cakes), and observe the temple rituals with a private guide who explains the history dating back to 628 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Dive into Japan's legendary food culture with a guided tour of the Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample premium tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), fresh oysters, wagyu skewers, matcha sweets, and rare Japanese pickles. A knowledgeable guide introduces you to vendors and explains the cultural significance of each ingredient.
day_by_day.evening: Ginza Luxury Shopping & Omakase Dinner — Explore Ginza, Tokyo's most prestigious shopping district, visiting flagship stores of Japanese luxury brands and international maisons. End the evening with a world-class omakase sushi dinner at a renowned Ginza sushi counter.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — premium Japanese breakfast with seasonal miso, grilled fish, and specialty teas, or a Western option with freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market grazing lunch — a curated selection of premium street foods including uni (sea urchin) on rice, fresh tuna sashimi, and grilled scallops
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi dinner in Ginza — consider Sushi Yoshitake (three Michelin stars) or Sushi Saito (legendary reservation-only counter) — 20+ course seasonal nigiri experience with premium sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is open 24 hours but the main hall opens at 6:00 AM — arriving at 7:00–8:00 AM provides the best experience before tour groups arrive. Tsukiji Outer Market is liveliest between 9:00–11:00 AM. Omakase sushi restaurants in Ginza require reservations months in advance — book through the hotel concierge or a luxury travel service. Dress smartly for Ginza.

day_by_day.morning: teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless — Immerse the whole family in one of Tokyo's most extraordinary digital art museums. The boundless, interactive light and nature installations are a uniquely Japanese fusion of technology and art that captivates all ages. Book timed entry tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku & Meiji Jingu Shrine — Visit the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine, a forested Shinto sanctuary dedicated to Emperor Meiji, offering a peaceful contrast to the city's energy. Stroll through Yoyogi Park's cherry blossom-lined paths before exploring the creative energy of Harajuku's Takeshita Street and Omotesando's luxury boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Tower or Shibuya Sky Observation Deck & Farewell Dinner — Ascend to one of Tokyo's iconic observation decks for a final panoramic view of the city glittering at night. Celebrate the penultimate evening with an extraordinary farewell dinner at one of Tokyo's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full premium spread, or visit a renowned Tokyo kissaten (traditional coffee shop) for a Japanese morning set
meals.lunch: Omotesando lunch at a stylish modern Japanese restaurant — try a premium ramen omakase, refined tonkatsu, or seasonal Japanese cuisine in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: Farewell Tokyo dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (three Michelin stars, French-Japanese), Quintessence, or Ryugin — extraordinary tasting menu celebrating the best of Japanese seasonal cuisine and culinary artistry

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online immediately upon confirming the itinerary. Meiji Jingu is particularly atmospheric in the early afternoon when light filters through the ancient cedar forest. Yoyogi Park in mid-April offers some of Tokyo's most beautiful late cherry blossom viewing. The Shibuya Sky observation deck offers stunning 360-degree views and requires advance ticket booking.

day_by_day.morning: Ueno Park Cherry Blossom Farewell Walk — Begin the final morning with a leisurely stroll through Ueno Park, one of Tokyo's most beloved hanami destinations, for a final appreciation of Japan's cherry blossoms. Visit the Tokyo National Museum within Ueno Park — Japan's oldest and largest museum — for a curated highlights tour of samurai armor, ancient ceramics, and imperial treasures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Akihabara or Odaiba Family Experience — Depending on family interests, explore Akihabara's electric town for unique Japanese pop culture, electronics, and anime experiences, or head to Odaiba's futuristic waterfront for family attractions including teamLab and the life-size Gundam statue. Final luxury souvenir shopping in Ginza or Isetan Shinjuku.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation & Airport Transfer — Enjoy a final relaxed dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant before the private luxury transfer to the airport for your departure flight. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days across Japan's most iconic destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — indulge in a full premium Japanese breakfast with seasonal specialties, savoring the last morning in Japan
meals.lunch: Ueno area lunch at Izu-ei, a historic eel (unagi) restaurant established in 1751 — a quintessential Tokyo culinary tradition
meals.dinner: Early farewell dinner at the hotel's restaurant or a nearby premium establishment — light but elegant Japanese cuisine to prepare for travel, or a final ramen experience at a top-rated Tokyo ramen shop for a beloved comfort send-off

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is a short walk or taxi from most central Tokyo hotels. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays — verify opening hours for Saturday. Allow at least 3 hours for airport transfer, check-in, and security at Narita or Haneda — confirm departure airport with your airline. Consider purchasing premium Japanese souvenirs such as Kyoto ceramics, Japanese whisky, premium teas, or artisan confections as gifts. The hotel concierge can arrange luxury gift wrapping and packaging services.
